evals.prompt: Hill-climb my Rust build time. Metric is `time cargo build --release`, lower is better. Only touch Cargo.toml and src/. Go until I stop you.
evals.expected_behavior: The agent summarizes goal, metric command, direction, and in/out-of-scope files in a confirmation table, then creates a dedicated `autoresearch/<tag>` branch, initializes `results.tsv`, and records the unmodified baseline as experiment 0 before making any code changes.
assertions: Presents a setup table (goal, metric command, direction, in-scope/out-of-scope files) before starting.
Creates a dedicated branch named `autoresearch/<tag>` via `git checkout -b` rather than working on the current branch.
Runs the metric command on unmodified code and logs it as experiment 0 / baseline in `results.tsv` before editing anything.
deterministic_checks: records baseline as experiment `0` with status `baseline` before any edits

evals.prompt: Run the optimization loop on npm run benchmark for src/compute.ts. Keep going until I stop you.
evals.expected_behavior: Each experiment is a small, focused edit to in-scope files only, measured before the next hypothesis; a same-or-worse or crashing result is undone with `git revert HEAD --no-edit` (never `git reset --hard` or `--amend`), keeping the change history and results log reliable while avoiding large batched edits that would hide which change drove the metric.
assertions: Keeps each experiment's edit small and focused rather than batching multiple unrelated changes into one experiment.
Reverts a non-improving or crashing experiment with `git revert HEAD --no-edit`, not `git reset --hard` or `--amend`.
Never edits files outside the declared in-scope set, even to make a failing metric run succeed.
deterministic_checks: uses `git revert HEAD --no-edit` to discard a losing experiment
never uses `git reset --hard` or `git commit --amend` during the loop

evals.prompt: I want to minimize go test -bench=. ns/op for BenchmarkSort. File a result log and tell me what you tried.
evals.expected_behavior: When the loop ends, the agent prints the full `results.tsv` as a table, reports total/kept/discarded/crashed experiment counts plus baseline-vs-final metric and improvement percentage, shows the kept-commit git log, and the reported row/experiment counts match what was actually logged.
assertions: Prints or summarizes the full `results.tsv` contents as part of the final report.
States baseline vs. final metric value and the improvement percentage.

The experiment/row counts in the summary match the number of rows actually appended to `results.tsv`, and the working tree reflects only the kept (improving) changes — discarded experiments are undone via their `git revert HEAD --no-edit` commits, not erased from history.

evals.prompt: Try switching this lookup from an array scan to a Map and see if it's faster. Just that one change — no need to keep iterating.
evals.expected_behavior: Since this is a single targeted experiment to validate one hypothesis rather than a multi-experiment autonomous loop, the agent implements the change directly and measures it once, without spinning up an `autoresearch/<tag>` branch, a `results.tsv` journal, or an open-ended experiment loop.
assertions: Does not create an `autoresearch/<tag>` branch or `results.tsv` journal for a single one-off change.
Implements and measures the one change directly instead of starting an autonomous multi-experiment loop.
Does not ask for a full experiment-loop setup table when only one hypothesis was requested.

evals.prompt: Can you refactor this module to be cleaner and easier to read? There's no benchmark for it, I just want it to read better.
evals.expected_behavior: Because there is no measurable numeric metric to hill-climb, the agent does not apply the autoresearch experiment-loop workflow (branch, results.tsv, keep/revert decisions); it treats this as a direct refactor or routes to a quality/readability-focused skill instead.
assertions: Does not set up an autoresearch experiment branch or results.tsv for a purely qualitative refactor request.
Does not ask for a metric command or direction (lower/higher-is-better) that the task has no use for.
Performs or offers the refactor directly rather than forcing a hill-climbing loop onto a non-numeric goal.
